for_you_if: you want extensive creative freedom for base building
you enjoy tense atmosphere during cave descents
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you require a fully explained narrative ending
you expect clear guidance for survival systems

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as prone to performance issues, citing low frame rates and the need for powerful hardware, alongside freezing and crashing problems.

citations.review_text: I'll start with the negatives so it doesn't seem like I don't like this game. The voice acting is terrible, and the story, while starting out good kinda goes off the rails near the end. This is also prevalent in the ending. Performance wise, this game is terrible as you need a supercomputer to even hope to get a steady 60 fps and like the first game its quite janky even if it is running at a steady framerate. That being said, the graphics are amazing and gameplay and sound design are both great. The monsters and atmosphere are perfectly designed, these two in conjunction making for a genuinely scary game. I definitely recommend.

Freezes up before I can even set a basecamp up. I tried reinstalling it. I tried putting graphics to lowest setting. I tried reaching out to support. So even though I actually love the new upgrades and would love to play it i just cant

Unoptimized piece of ♥♥♥♥. I played this game with my GF and despite the fact that I have way above the recommended specs, I would still crash or occasionally lag while playing the game (I was the one hosting if that matters). In my opinion, the game itself is also just objectively worse than the first game. The lore doesn't really get expanded on, and the story is pretty mid anyways. The gameplay is the main issue we both had with this game. The game throws a bunch of erratic, enemies that move at mach ♥♥♥♥ at you that don't recieve any stun from being hit, this makes the early game especially a nightmare, as you don't have any armor and are low on meds. So the early game is absolutely miserable where you die constantly because the bow isn't an option because it's way harder to aim than the first game and the enemies move way too fast for it to be of any use anyways. The second-to-final boss also sucked, it just being an upscaled bullet sponge enemy. Endnight really got lazy making this game and put all their budget on the graphics.

No idea why people think this game is so good. It has some entertainment value but I would be hard-pressed to call it good. The story didn't really make any sense to me as a casual player and the gameplay felt pretty clunky. There's virtually no reason to go through the tedium of building a base beyond something very basic and all the vehicles are pretty much pointless due to the existence of the foldable glider. I didn't find the ending very satisfying either. For a supposed horror game it isn't really all that scary—the bat jumpscares don't get any better with repetition. Having your teammates die just the moment you find them every single time becomes a pretty major immersion-breaker, same with helicopters leaving every single time just as you find them. I don't think this game really has any redeemable qualities. It's entertaining but not good.

Also very disappointed with the endgame fight. The progression being very slow in the first game was fixed here with computer chips and gps or some ♥♥♥♥ every bunker lead to another. Also the minimap was necessary. I still stand by what I said about the lore and the ending. There is some serious work that the studio needs to do about the third game. A huge explanation and better/final ending is expected of the third game.
its very conveluted tedius and the ending just suck would not recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers find the building and crafting systems clunky or difficult to use, specifically noting problems with roof work, lack of ladders, and inconsistent mechanics.

citations.review_text: The game is poorly balanced. The build system is *almost* enjoyable, if not for the CONSTANT assaults by cannibals hell bent on undoing all your work. And also the lack of ladders. Positioning yourself for doing work on roofs is awful.

The gameplay is clunky as hell. The inventory system is nice at first for immersion, but becomes annoying to deal with. The story is straight-up not good. I didn't really see a point in building a base either, we built one and never returned, because you have to get around the whole island to progress, there is no reason to return anyway, as you have everything in the invertory anyway. The system for building is good, but it's just pointless to build anything other than immersion. The driving is pretty bad too.

The lack of an autosave feature is also frustrating. I don't wanna be building tents everywhere just in case the game crashes.

The game is, so far, very interesting, but to be honest i do not like the new building mechanic.
I find it to be very clunky and inconsistent at times and i am not even going to get started on Kelvin.
Other than that i am enjoying the game and it stays loyal to what The Forest had to offer, it's the same style, same gameplay (almost) as the first game.
I would recommend it if you likes The Forest.

I never leave reviews, but we just wrapped up this game and... wow. Had fun along the way, to be fair, but I'm never revisiting this clunky mess unlike the first game.

Survival was trivial after the first day. Combat was easy if using ranged options, impossible if going melee only later on. Base building was fun enough, but ultimately unnecessary for any sort of progress since MREs/sodas were so plentiful. Item locations were random/nonsensical, IE the compound bow and crossbow. The mutants were gross, which was a big plus, but the final boss was a complete joke.

The ending was HORRIBLE and didn't seem like there was any reasonable buildup to it. No moral dilemma, no capstone idea or anything... Sorta felt like Star Wars sequels. What the hell was that, who the hell are you, why should I care (I don't), and oh okay I guess we're done. The decision to stay or leave the island in the first game was one that actually mattered: sacrifice someone else to save your son, or commit to staying on the island so no one else would suffer. This one? Nah, stay so you can keep the collectible and base build, or leave so you can get tf out of there. 

Also knocking up Virginia was really, really, really weird. Do better Endnight.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from bugs and a lack of polish.

citations.review_text: Yes I've played it a fair bit. And yes it has strong points. But 3 years after release and it is riddled with bugs, lacks polish, and shows all the signs of a company just doing a 1.0 cash grab and getting the f outta dodge. I don't care if it's an indie studio - they've made an estimated 250 mil. That's more than enough to spend an extra 6 months polishing things up proper or even hiring a studio to do it. Shame on the devs.

I loved the first one, it was far to be perfect and a lot of mistakes, pretty annoying building and craft system, but the story was pretty nice, condensed and hard to lost yourself to continue.
This one is weirdly exactly the same thing, scaled by 10 in size and features, but with the same unfinished and unpolished gameplay, worse game design, the achievement to make the worse caves' level design ever and a story written by a kid that make absolutely no sense.

I don't even know if the devs couldn't be bother to finish it or they ran out of money at this point, the foundation are great, it's missing everything else.

I'm pretty sure people that left good review for that game never finished it, they had fun for the first 5-10hrs, then gave up, but the product as the whole is very bad, especially compared to The Forest that was very good.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the building and structure customization is improved and provides extensive creative freedom for base design.

citations.review_text: I love how customisable the building and structures have become. They have basically taken everything I loved about The Forest and improved on it all!

I like that this game still manages to surprise me. Even after hundreds of hours, I'm constantly discovering new mechanics, interactions, or little details I never knew existed.

The building system is where the game really shines. There's so much room for creativity that I'll often spend an entire evening experimenting with new designs instead of making any "progress." Building stops feeling like a necessity for survival and becomes its own game.

What I appreciate most is that there isn't any pressure to rush the story. You can spend hours—or even days—exploring, hunting, gathering resources, expanding your base, or simply enjoying the island before touching the main plot. The game lets you set your own pace, and that freedom makes the world feel far more believable than survival games that constantly push you toward the next objective.

The island feels like a place to inhabit rather than a checklist to complete, and that's why I keep coming back.

10/10 

One of the best base-building/survival games you can buy and buy again to gift a friend.
<3

My Sons of the Forest Review (as a SOTF Nerd)

Gameplay: 9/10
This game has improved a lot compared to the previous one (The Forest). So many mechanics received upgrades. The combat feels much smoother thanks to the dismemberment system, not to mention the unique building system, which is probably the coolest I've ever seen in a game.

Story: 6/10
The story isn't one of the game's strongest points. There are still so many unanswered questions and a few plot holes. I still enjoy it despite those issues, and I think a future game could expand on the lore and fix many of these problems.

Graphics: 10/10
Bruh... this is easily the most beautiful game in my Steam library. There's not much else to say, it just looks absolutely stunning.

Audio: 8/10
I don't usually pay much attention to audio in the games I play, but Sons of the Forest has some really immersive ambient sounds. The only reason I'm giving it an 8 is because the proximity voice chat is buns.

Performance: 8/10
I'm not exactly sure how well optimized Sons of the Forest is, but I have friends who were able to play it at a solid framerate even with weaker PCs. I think performance depends a lot on how you manage your graphics settings, because there are many options that don't make a noticeable visual difference but can significantly lower your FPS.

World Design: 7/10
Don't get me wrong, the island is beautiful, and the cannibal villages are cool. But after around, let's say, 100 hours, the world starts to feel... empty? In The Forest, the map was much smaller, so the developers could put more attention into details, create more unique villages, and make each location feel memorable. In Sons of the Forest, many villages and camps feel repetitive, and a huge part of the map is just forest (obviously). I still like it, but I wish there were more interesting landmarks and structures to discover.

Another thing I preferred in the first game was how all the caves were connected in some way. In Sons of the Forest, mo…

Sons of the Forest takes everything that made The Forest great and improves on it. The graphics are incredible, the atmosphere is tense, and exploring the island always feels rewarding. The changing seasons and weather make survival more immersive, while the improved building system gives you much more freedom to create unique bases. While the game has improved considerably since launch, occasional bugs and AI quirks can still disrupt immersion. Several mechanics could have been expanded with future updates. Unfortunately, the developers have moved on, leaving the game in a state that feels complete enough to play, but not complete enough to reach its full potential Rating: 4/5 cat bells 🔔🔔🔔🔔

citations.review_text: The game is somewhat fun, bringing many new features, but is also lacking many features seen in the first game? Take for example, setting weapons on fire with cloth, such a simple feature that is just missing. The building system is very interesting and enjoyable... when it works that is. It is very messy and often requires utilizing glitches and/or "bargaining" with the building system to make anything more complex than a box shaped shed. The friendly AIs are a disappointment, with them being incredibly simple and more often than not just a burden instead of help. The story is just horrible, not to mention boring. I really hate the sci-fi direction they took towards the mid to late game and the one they´re continuing with to the third game. The map is too large for its own good, with the only option of transport that doesn´t make me want to altf4 is the glider. The game feels unfinished and placeholder-y, despite it being a full release and seemingly finished with content drops or even just bug patches.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the atmosphere as tense and immersive, particularly during nighttime exploration and cave descents.

citations.review_text:
🩸 THE SAGA OF RINO THE VIKING: SONS OF THE FOREST 🩸

I arrived on the island in a helicopter with a trained team, modern equipment and a clear mission.

Several minutes later, the helicopter was in pieces, most of the team was missing and I was standing in the wilderness beside a confused man named Kelvin.

It was not the expedition we had planned.

Sons of the Forest drops you into a beautiful island that immediately begins trying to kill you. Dense forests hide hostile tribes. Peaceful beaches conceal evidence that something has gone terribly wrong. Beneath the ground, dark caves descend into places where flashlights, ammunition and courage all seem to run out at the same time.

After 123 hours, the game’s greatest strength remains its atmosphere.

The island can feel strangely peaceful during the day. You gather supplies, cut timber, build shelter and watch the seasons transform the landscape around you. Then night falls, something moves between the trees and every sound beyond the fire becomes a possible warning.

Exploration constantly creates tension. Abandoned camps, underground facilities and cave entrances promise valuable equipment, but discovering what waits inside usually requires descending into darkness with limited resources and no guarantee that the return journey will be easy.

The caves are where Sons of the Forest becomes true survival horror.

Narrow passages restrict movement. Batteries begin to fade. Ammunition becomes precious. Shapes crawl through the darkness, and the confidence you carried underground gradually disappears with every unexplained sound.

Building provides a welcome contrast to the horror. The flexible construction system allows you to create anything from a crude shelter to an enormous fortified settlement. Placing individual logs can be slower than using a traditional blueprint system, but it also makes every wall, tower and defensive barrier feel like something you genuinely constructed.

Unfortunately…

It puts in that surviaval mode where you are checking over your shoulder very minute as it always feels like someone or something is stalking/watching you from the trees. It feels like I am playing the show LOST. I give this game a fat 9/10 as it can be a little confusing when it comes to understading how to progress in the story. Other than that fantastic game, went in thinking it was gonna be very generic but it blew me away. Good job!

In The Forest, the map was much smaller, so the developers could put more attention into details, create more unique villages, and make each location feel memorable. In Sons of the Forest, many villages and camps feel repetitive, and a huge part of the map is just forest (obviously). I still like it, but I wish there were more interesting landmarks and structures to discover.
